title: Analysis code for: Culture-proven neonatal infection: lower total bilirubin and an erythrocyte signature confined to definite pathogens
description:
Version 1.7.7 is a metadata and packaging release; no analysis code, numeric result, table or figure changed. It (i) adds a manuscript-figure to script-output mapping table to 00_Code_Index_and_Run_Order.md (script fig5() produces manuscript Figure 4; script fig6() produces manuscript Figure 5; script fig4() is retained but not used, because the Mendelian-randomisation layer was removed from this manuscript), (ii) annotates those three functions in 20261009_manuscript_figures.R accordingly, (iii) corrects the repository name to IL6_HEPCIDIN, and (iv) clarifies the script inventory (61 analysis scripts plus 2 utility scripts). Users who only need to reproduce the published numbers may use v1.7.6 without loss.

Version 1.7.6 corrected the Fig. 2a plotting-input CSV (fig2A_bilirubin_mimic3_ascii.csv): the definite-pathogen and CoNS-only rows still held pre-1.7.3 stratum counts (19 / 46; -2.11 / -0.55 mg/dL) although the analysis scripts, code index and manuscript had all used the unified pathogen rule (20 / 45; -2.08 / -0.61 mg/dL). The published Fig. 2a and Table 1 are unchanged; this release only makes the archived plotting data reproduce them.

Analysis code (63 files: 54 analysis Python scripts, 7 analysis R scripts, and 2 utility scripts, md2docx_generic.py and run_abf2.R; plus the plotting-input CSV files) reproducing every number, table and figure reported in the manuscript. The code covers two neonatal clinical cohorts (MIMIC-IV v1.0 and MIMIC-III v1.4), the measurement-level phototherapy-mediation analysis, the within-subject 48 h/72 h replication of the paired culture-anchored design in MIMIC-IV, human hepatocyte transcriptomes from GEO, and the APR-DRG birth-weight-band coverage sensitivity reported as the last row of Table S2. Mendelian randomisation and colocalisation scripts from earlier versions are retained for audit but are not reported in this version.

No patient-level data are redistributed. MIMIC-III and MIMIC-IV are access-controlled on PhysioNet and require credentialed access together with acceptance of the data use agreement; the clinical scripts expect a local PostgreSQL instance holding the MIMIC schemas. All other inputs (GEO) are public.

See 00_Code_Index_and_Run_Order.md for the script-by-script index, the recommended run order, runtime pitfalls, and a table mapping each manuscript number to its source script. The development repository is at https://github.com/ruijin1/IL6_HEPCIDIN.

Version 1.7.5 adds the MIMIC-IV cross-sectional replication of the erythrocyte signature (Table S8; Fig. 3c): 1,132 admissions, definite-pathogen MCV -2.08 fL and MCH -0.63 pg, CoNS-only null, RDW null, about half the MIMIC-III effect size. Version 1.7.4 corrected the culture-to-measurement interval analysis to the unified pathogen rule (45 definite-pathogen admissions, 23 with a post-culture measurement; median 2.5 days, IQR 1.7-3.1). Version 1.7.3 applied one pathogen-class rule to both cohorts: a culture is coagulase-negative only when every organism reported is a coagulase-negative staphylococcus, so the MIMIC-III stratum estimates change slightly (definite 19 -> 20 pairs, 42 -> 45 admissions).
